y2 <- c(4, .8, .5, .45, .4, .3)

par(las=1, mar=c(4, 4, 2, 4), cex=.7)

# Persp
x <- seq(-10, 10, length= 30); y <- x
f <- function(x,y) { r <- sqrt(x^2+y^2); 10 * sin(r)/r }
z <- outer(x, y, f); z[is.na(z)] <- 1
par(mar=c(0, 0.5, 0, 0), lwd=0.5)

1.1 Choose one of the six charts and explain

Barplot with VADeaths — key steps: (1) adjust margins for compact labels, (2) draw stacked bars with grayscale, (3) place multi-line group labels in the margin, (4) add centered counts using cumulative sums, and (5) reset par(mar=...) so later plots are unaffected.

lm1 <- lm(y1 ~ x1, data=anscombe)
lm2 <- lm(y2 ~ x2, data=anscombe)
lm3 <- lm(y3 ~ x3, data=anscombe)
lm4 <- lm(y4 ~ x4, data=anscombe)

2.1 Compare the regression models

All four have nearly identical slopes/intercepts and R², yet the patterns differ (nonlinearity, outliers, leverage). See plots below.

4 How about with ggplot2? (use tidyverse)

Code 
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly=TRUE) ||
    !requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly=TRUE) ||
    !requireNamespace("tidyr", quietly=TRUE) ||
    !requireNamespace("broom", quietly=TRUE)) {
  message("Install: ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, broom")
} else {
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(broom)

  anscombe_long <- anscombe %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
                 names_to = c(".value","set"),
                 names_pattern = "(.)(.)") %>%
    mutate(set = as.integer(set))

  coefs <- anscombe_long %>%
    group_by(set) %>%
    do(tidy(lm(y ~ x, data = .))) %>%
    select(set, term, estimate) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>%
    rename(intercept = `(Intercept)`, slope = x)

  lines <- anscombe_long %>%
    group_by(set) %>%
    summarise(x = seq(min(x), max(x), length.out=100), .groups="drop") %>%
    left_join(coefs, by="set") %>%
    mutate(y = intercept + slope * x)

  ggplot(anscombe_long, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
    geom_point(shape=8, size=3, color="darkolivegreen3") +
    geom_line(data=lines, aes(x=x, y=y),
              color="goldenrod3", linetype="dashed", linewidth=1) +
    facet_wrap(~set, ncol=2, labeller = labeller(set = function(i) paste("Dataset", i))) +
    theme_minimal(base_family="serif") +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(color="darkgreen", face="bold", size=16, hjust=0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(color="darkgreen", face="bold"),
      axis.text = element_text(color="darkolivegreen4"),
      axis.ticks = element_line(color="darkolivegreen4"),
      panel.border = element_rect(color="darkolivegreen3", fill=NA, linewidth=0.8),
      strip.text = element_text(color="forestgreen", face="bold", size=12)
    ) +
    labs(title="Anscombe's Quartet — Styled ggplot2", x="X values", y="Y values")
}

5 Pre-hackathon by team:

Code 
# Robust OWID ingest
owidall <- read.csv(
  "https://github.com/owid/covid-19-data/blob/master/public/data/owid-covid-data.csv?raw=true",
  na.strings = c("", "NA", "N/A", "NaN", "nan", "null", "NULL", "Inf", "-Inf")
)
owidall <- subset(owidall, !grepl("^OWID", iso_code))
owidall$date <- as.Date(owidall$date)

# Europe subset (fallback to whitelist if needed)
owideu <- subset(owidall, continent == "Europe")
if (nrow(owideu) == 0) {
  eu_names <- c("Albania","Andorra","Armenia","Austria","Azerbaijan","Belarus","Belgium",
                "Bosnia and Herzegovina","Bulgaria","Croatia","Cyprus","Czechia","Denmark",
                "Estonia","Finland","France","Georgia","Germany","Greece","Hungary","Iceland",
                "Ireland","Italy","Kazakhstan","Kosovo","Latvia","Liechtenstein","Lithuania",
                "Luxembourg","Malta","Moldova","Monaco","Montenegro","Netherlands",
                "North Macedonia","Norway","Poland","Portugal","Romania","Russia","San Marino",
                "Serbia","Slovakia","Slovenia","Spain","Sweden","Switzerland","Turkey",
                "Ukraine","United Kingdom","Vatican")
  owideu <- subset(owidall, location %in% eu_names)
}

# Last non-NA snapshot per country × indicator
candidates <- c(
  "total_cases_per_million",
  "total_deaths_per_million",
  "people_vaccinated_per_hundred",
  "people_fully_vaccinated_per_hundred",
  "total_tests_per_thousand",
  "life_expectancy",
  "median_age",
  "hospital_beds_per_thousand",
  "stringency_index",
  "diabetes_prevalence",
  "cvd_death_rate"
)
candidates <- intersect(candidates, names(owideu))

last_non_na <- function(x) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  tail(x, 1)
}

by_cty <- split(owideu, owideu$location)
eu_last <- do.call(rbind, lapply(by_cty, function(d) {
  setNames(as.data.frame(t(sapply(candidates, function(v) last_non_na(d[[v]])))), candidates)
}))
row.names(eu_last) <- names(by_cty)

# Keep only indicators with any finite values
eu_last <- eu_last[, sapply(eu_last, function(x) any(is.finite(x))), drop = FALSE]

# Auto-pick up to 6 best-covered indicators
cov_tbl <- sort(sapply(eu_last, function(x) sum(is.finite(x))), decreasing = TRUE)
keep_vars <- names(cov_tbl)[cov_tbl >= 10][1:min(6, sum(cov_tbl >= 10))]
if (length(keep_vars) < 2) keep_vars <- names(cov_tbl)[cov_tbl >= 5][1:min(6, sum(cov_tbl >= 5))]
if (length(keep_vars) < 2) {
  stop("Not enough finite data for any two indicators. Coverage: ",
       paste(names(cov_tbl)[cov_tbl > 0], collapse = ", "))
}

eu_mat <- eu_last[, keep_vars, drop = FALSE]

# Final guard
eu_mat <- eu_mat[, sapply(eu_mat, function(x) any(is.finite(x))), drop = FALSE]
if (ncol(eu_mat) < 2) stop("Only one indicator has finite values after filtering.")

pairs(
  eu_mat,
  main = paste0("COVID-19 Europe — SPLOM (", paste(colnames(eu_mat), collapse = ", "), ")"),
  pch = 21, bg = "gray80", col = "gray40", cex = 1
)

(Optional) Labelled time-series of daily deaths peaks (ggplot2) — guarded

Code 
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly=TRUE)) {
  library(ggplot2); library(dplyr)
  owideu2 <- subset(owidall, !grepl("^OWID", iso_code) & continent=="Europe")
  owideu2$date <- as.Date(owideu2$date)

  if (!"new_deaths_smoothed" %in% names(owideu2)) {
    message("new_deaths_smoothed not present in this OWID snapshot; skipping the labeled plot.")
  } else {
    label_countries <- c("Spain","Germany","Ukraine","Italy")
    owideu2 <- subset(owideu2, !is.na(new_deaths_smoothed))
    label_points <- owideu2 |>
      dplyr::filter(location %in% label_countries) |>
      dplyr::group_by(location) |>
      dplyr::slice_max(order_by = new_deaths_smoothed, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
      dplyr::ungroup()

    ggplot(owideu2, aes(x=date, y=new_deaths)) +
      geom_point(shape=16, size=1.1, alpha=0.7) +
      geom_text(data=label_points, aes(label=location), vjust=-0.6, size=3) +
      scale_x_date(date_breaks = "4 months", date_labels = "%Y-%m") +
      labs(x="Date", y="COVID Deaths in Europe (Daily)", title="Selected Countries — Peak Daily Deaths") +
      theme_classic(base_family="serif") +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=60, hjust=1, size=9))
  }
}
